Time Clauses
You can use different time conjunctions to describe events in the past, present and future. You can also express events that happen at the same time, and events that happen one after the other.

Simultaneous Actions:
as/when/while ➡ for longer actions in progress in the background when another action happens. Progressive tenses are usually used with these words.
when + the simple past in the time clause and a main clause action in a progressive tense ➡ shows interruption. The action in the time clause interrupts the action in the main clause.
while ➡ with two longer situations happening at the same time

Consecutive Actions:
when + past simple in the time clause and past simple in the main clause ➡ an action happening right after another. When expresses the first action.
as ➡ two short events that happen at almost the same time.
once + present perfect ➡ if something has to be completed before something else can happen
before ➡ for an action that occurred before something else happened
until ➡ when the first action happens up to the time of the second action.

Past Actions or Events:
when ➡ for something that happened at a particular time in the past
before, after, as soon as ➡ with these expressions especially, the order of events is clear.
time conjunction + past perfect ➡ to emphasize the completion of one action (the one in the past perfect) before another

Present Actions or Events:
present simple in both clauses ➡ for actions that are generally true. Similar to the zero conditional.

Future Actions or Events:
time expression + present simple verb, future verb in main clause ➡ for future events/actions
time expression + present perfect, future verb in main clause ➡ for specific situations where it is necessary to know the time order of the events
The Anderson group will come in as soon as everyone in their party arrives.
When I am here, I am always thirsty!
Amy, while I'm working tonight, I am also delegating more management duties this evening.
We had talked it over for about five minutes before we came out tonight.
Ever since Vanessa and I have been meeting, I feel like we have made some real progress.
The Unreal Past: Second, Third and Mixed Conditional
You can talk about past, present and future events that are not real by using different conditional structures in your sentences.

Vanessa: Welcome guys! Come sit down. Chill out. Don't worry. The Anderson group will come in as soon as everyone in their party arrives. So, I can hangout a little bit tonight before our big party arrives later.
Peter: What are we drinking?
Vanessa: Wine, from our new supplier. I had talked to the old supplier for about ten minutes today, but I felt that if we had stayed with them, we would have had more late shipments and more thirsty customers.
Peter: Exactly! When I am here, I am always thirsty!
Vanessa: Amy, while I'm working tonight, I am also delegating more management duties this evening. I wouldn't have been so close to burning out, if I had just relaxed a little more. I have burned the candle at both ends for far too long.
Amy: Good to hear. Ever since Vanessa and I have been meeting, I feel like we have made some real progress.

Vanessa: Yes, indeed. Also before the night shift, the staff and I had discussed things before and we had a real heart to heart. I convinced Rachel, Michael and Alexander to come back. We agreed to be more conscientious toward each other's feelings. Ahhh! If I had worked harder at school, I would have a better job than I do now.
Peter: Haha, and if you went to bed earlier you wouldn't be so tired all the time, but that's not happening.
Vanessa: True, but seriously, I think we would have resolved our problems if I had just listened a little more closely. I had just kept everything bottled up before, but now I'm going to try and be more amiable.

Peter: Well, Amy and I have some news too. We had talked it over for about five minutes before we came out tonight. I suppose we have waited a little longer than we should have.
Vanessa: Let me guess, you two are dating.
Peter: How did you know?
Vanessa: Have you ever wondered why the two of you connected again?
Peter: Huh?
Vanessa: Oh yeah. Amy wouldn't have come to the bar that night if I hadn't asked her.
Peter: Really?
Amy: Peter you are so cute.
Vanessa: If Amy hadn't said anything, I would have toyed with you for the rest of the night. Anyway, raise a glass. Before we get carried away, I want to make a toast. To friends.
Amy and Peter: To friends!
Vanessa: You guys are the best!
